To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
legal rules governing flood defenses are generally well adapted to the need for adaptation to change.
the legal frameworks for flood defense infrastructures are in many respects not fit for purpose, but there are some signs of progress.

(1) there is a trend towards clearer and, in some cases, more powerful public authorities to ensure the safety and maintenance of flood defense infrastructure; (2) there is evidence of a shift in the focus of the legal rules on flood defense infrastructure towards the consideration of change and uncertainty in the development of new flood defense infrastructure; however, (3) the adaptation of existing flood defense infrastructure is a more complex matter and the legal rules fail to adequately deal with the damages caused by external events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which the law allows for the adaptive management of flood defense infrastructure.
how legal rules can support adaptive governance in flood defense infrastructure, which is essential to the resilience of the water system.
the extent to which national legal rules allow for response and adaptive governance of flood defense infrastructure to change and uncertainty in flood risks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the law should be more adaptive and flexible, and that the law should also be more adaptive and resilient to the impacts of climate change and climate variability.

legal rules should be developed that ensure that decisions to build, operate and maintain flood defenses are based upon a holistic assessment of the risks and benefits, and are made in a way that is responsive to changing circumstances and uncertainties.
legal rules governing flood defenses are generally not well equipped to address the challenges of change and uncertainty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need to develop a more integrated approach to the management of flood risks, and to the legal rules that govern this process, in particular in relation to the operation and maintenance of existing infrastructure.
the legal frameworks for flood defense are not yet sufficiently adaptive to deal with increasing flood risks.
the law can be used as an instrument of change and adaptation to the new challenges posed by climate change and increasing flood risks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the law can be an enabler for adaptation to climate change, but it is only one of many tools that can be used to achieve this goal.
the law should facilitate adaptation, rather than constrain it.
the law can be used to promote adaptive governance in flood defense infrastructure, and that the law is an important instrument for achieving resilience.
